sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
The pad area is identical to the first frame (no diff shown — all blank). So the pad doesn't visually change. Both bars are fully extended. Level incomplete.
Time to rethink the objective from scratch. Elements:
1. Green bar (top, horizontal), cap on left (col 27), body cols 28–62, dot at col 61. Marker at col 52.
2. Yellow bar (left, vertical), cap at top (row 27), body rows 28–62, dot at row 61. Marker at row 52.
3. Yellow battery pack (2 cells), green battery pack (2 cells).
4. Dots at both ends of the bar… wait, no, the dots: each bar has exactly one dot.
Hmm, what does "clearing the level" mean? Maybe: the dots have to line up / return to the start? Or: the dot's position has to match something (e.g., the marker's position)?
Or, the intended objective might be something else: the bar is a "candy bar" / "battery gauge", and the pad is the charger. The marker is the "target position": the dot has to land exactly on the marker (col 52 / row 52) — i.e., the bar's length has to be 25 (28+24, dot at 51)? Hmm, the dot is one before the end: dot 52 ↔ end 53.
Green: end 53 = 26 cols from 28. Yellow same.
Currently green end = 62. To get end 53: 9 drain clicks (left pad). Yellow: end 35 → wait, yellow end is currently 62; to get to 53: 9 drain clicks (top pad).
But is that the goal? The marker is at 52; the dot on top of the marker's center (10,52)/(52,10): dot col 52 ↔ end 53. Hmm, why would that be the goal? The marker looks like a "crosshair" / target.
Or, the goal: dot touches the marker's arm: dot 51 ↔ end 52: 10 drain.
Or, the goal is that the bar passes the marker exactly, and the dot ends up on the far side… currently green dot = 61, marker center = 52: the dot is 9 past the marker.
Another idea: maybe the game wants the two dots to be at the same "position" along their respective axes (relative distance from start): currently both dots at index 34 (col 61 / row 61) — already identical! And yet incomplete.
Maybe the dots need to be at the same absolute… they're on different axes, so impossible.
Maybe the goal involves the cap: shrink the bar so the dot reaches the cap? Dot adjacent to the cap: end 28, dot 28?? A length-1 bar: single-cell dot? Green: drain from 62 to 28: 34 clicks. Yellow: 34. Total 68 > timer 28. Impossible. Timer: 64-36=28 steps remaining. So the solution has to be within about 28 actions.
Options within budget:
(a) Drain 9 each (18 total): dots at 52, 62… wait, green dot 61 → drain 9 → end 53, dot 52 = marker center. Yellow same: dot 52. Both dots exactly at the marker center. Elegant! Total 18 actions ≤ 28.
(b) Drain 10 each: dots at 51 (the marker's arm row/col). 20 actions.
(c) Some other arrangement of fill/drain.
I like (a): the plus marker is a target, and the dot should land on its center. The plus center is B (black) — maybe when the dot lands on it, it becomes "captured" / turns into something, and the level completes.
Actually wait: when the bar passed through the marker, the center became N/Y (bar color), and the arms remained r. The center is now the same color as the bar — meaning the marker's center is effectively a hole in the bar? No, it's a separate node but the same color, visually connected.
Hmm, let me reconsider: the dot is the "charge" that should be delivered to the battery pack? The pack is in the center of the board. No visible connection.
Another thought: maybe the objective is to have both dots exactly on top of the marker center simultaneously (a symmetric "aiming" puzzle). (a) achieves that: green dot col 52, yellow dot row 52.
Or, the objective: the dots are both… hmm.
Let me also consider (d): drain both bars to length 1 (dot at 28) — impossible within budget.
(e): Make both bars the same length as each other in cell count — they already are (both 35 cols, minus 1 for the dot… both have a dot). Incomplete.
(f): Maybe the level completes when both dots are on top of their respective markers AND the bars are of equal length. (a) satisfies equal length (both 26) and the dot-on-center condition.
Going with (a): 9 drain clicks on green left pad (21,39), 9 on yellow top pad (38,24). 18 actions. If it doesn't complete after the first 9 (green dot at 52), I'll evaluate then (maybe I need to match the yellow too, or a different offset).
Wait, actually, before the big drain, let me reconsider the possibility that the dot-on-center offset is 51 instead of 52. The marker center (B) is at (10,52): if the dot lands there, the dot pixel at (10,52) would overwrite… The center is currently N (green). The dot is r. If the dot is at col 52, the pixel (10,52) becomes r.
The arms are r at (9,52), (10,51), (10,53), (11,52). If the dot is at 52: the r at 52 joins with the arms → the marker is completed again as a full plus? That's aesthetically the "goal state": the dot completes the plus. If the dot is at 51: the r's would be at 51, 52?? No: the dot at 51 would replace the r at (10,51) (no visible change!), the marker would stay as is. Visually uneventful.
So (a) with the dot at 52 is the "dot completes the plus" state.
Plan: 9 clicks on green left pad, check; then 9 on yellow top pad.
Actually, to save turns, do green 9 + check + yellow 9 + check in one Python run.
